caption: A steel cocktail shaker filled with ice is shaken, and its outside turns white with frost within seconds.

sa.check: A steel cocktail shaker is filled with ice.
Its outside turns white with frost.
The frost is thickest over the part the ice fills.
The shaking comes first and the frost follows.

pc.expect: The frost appears on the shaker's outside while it is shaken with ice inside, thickest over the part the ice fills.
pc.fail: The frost appears before the shaking starts; or the shaker is shaken with ice in it and its outside stays bright and dry to the end of the clip; or the frost appears on the cap while the body over the ice stays bright; or the frost appears on the hands rather than the metal.

pc.expect: The frost only builds while the shaker stays cold and any later change is toward wetness as it warms.
pc.fail: The frost thickens, goes and thickens again while the shaking goes on; or wet drops turn back into dry white frost as the shaker warms; or the frost retreats while the ice is still inside; or the frost thins and thickens in turn.

pc.expect: Once the frost turns to drops they run downward on the shaker's sides and drip from its base.
pc.fail: A drop runs up the shaker; or water gathers on the cap's top and stays as a dome; or a drop leaves the shaker and rises; or a run travels sideways round the shaker and stays level.

pc.expect: The frost is a fine white bloom on the metal that softens into beads, and the shaker stays a rigid steel vessel.
pc.fail: The frost stands off as thick spikes of ice; or the frost peels away as a sheet; or the shaker's metal flexes as it is shaken; or the frost sets as a hard glaze that stays dry as the shaker warms.

pc.expect: One shaker with its cap on; the shaker keeps its shape and nothing passes through it.
pc.fail: The shaker changes shape; or a second shaker appears; or the cap passes into the body; or ice passes out through the steel.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The shaker's finish away from the frost, the hands and the bar stay the same.
pc.fail: The shaker changes colour; or the bar's bottles rearrange; or the background changes between frames.

note: The hands are kept because the shaking is the caption's action; they are otherwise not judged.
